curation.lead:
Ehud Barak, Israel’s 10th Prime Minister and former Chief of the IDF General Staff, occupies a unique position in the Jeffrey Epstein network: he is simultaneously the highest-ranking foreign head of state and the most prolific correspondent in the DOJ email corpus. With 1,411 files in a dedicated email archive—more than any other bilateral correspondence except Michael Wolff’s—the Barak-Epstein relationship was not peripheral. It was structural. The communications span business strategy for Carbyne, intelligence briefings from Russian officials at SPIEF, introductions to Qatari royals, and scheduling of regular in-person meetings in New York through at least late 2017.

The financial architecture binding the two men ran through multiple channels. The Wexner Foundation paid Barak $2.3 million between 2004 and 2006 for two research papers—one of which was never completed—during the exact period Epstein served as de facto CFO of the Wexner family office. Later, Epstein invested in Carbyne through his Southern Trust Company (STC), holding 66.67% of the investment vehicle SUM (E.B.) Limited Partnership while Barak served as general partner with carried interest. When Israeli anti-money-laundering lawyers sought to identify STC’s controlling person, Epstein’s attorney Darren Indyke resisted disclosure.

Beyond finance, Barak served as a bridge between the Israeli private intelligence ecosystem and the Epstein network. He introduced Harvey Weinstein to Black Cube, the Mossad-veteran intelligence firm that deployed covert operatives against Weinstein’s accusers and journalists. As chairman of Carbyne—an emergency call technology company with surveillance implications—Barak pitched the product to Qatari former Prime Minister Hamad bin Jassim Al Thani for 2022 World Cup security, offering to “minimize the Israeli profile.” Epstein brokered the introduction. The pattern is consistent: Barak provided geopolitical access and intelligence credibility; Epstein provided capital, introductions, and operational infrastructure.

sections.title: Intelligence and Military Background
sections.content:
Ehud Barak (born Ehud Brog, February 12, 1942, Kibbutz Mishmar HaSharon) rose through the Israeli military to its highest operational and command positions. He headed IDF Military Intelligence (Aman), served as Chief of the General Staff from 1991 to 1995, and was Israel’s most decorated soldier. His military career included command of the elite Sayeret Matkal special forces unit. After retiring from the military, he served as Minister of Foreign Affairs (1995–1996), was elected Prime Minister in 1999, and later served as Minister of Defense and Deputy Prime Minister under Netanyahu (2007–2013).

This background is essential context for his post-government activities. Barak’s intelligence credentials were not merely biographical decoration—they were functional assets deployed in his relationship with Epstein. OpenSanctions designates him a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) across multiple categories: diplomatic, military, and political. This PEP status meant that every financial institution handling Barak-related transactions—Deutsche Bank, Bank Leumi, Wells Fargo—was legally obligated to apply enhanced due diligence. Multiple banks flagged these requirements, yet the financial relationships persisted.

His connections to Israeli private intelligence firms, particularly Black Cube (founded by former Mossad and Aman officers), were direct. Barak admitted to introducing Harvey Weinstein to Black Cube, though he claimed the introduction was “unwitting.” Black Cube subsequently deployed Mossad-style covert operations against Weinstein’s accusers and journalists investigating abuse allegations. Whether Barak’s role was truly inadvertent or part of a broader pattern of leveraging Israeli intelligence capabilities for private-sector clients remains an open question.

sections.title: Epstein Financial Relationship
sections.content:
The financial relationship between Barak and Epstein operated through at least three distinct channels, each with its own corporate vehicle and jurisdictional logic.

Wexner Foundation grants (2004–2006): The Wexner Foundation paid Barak $2.3 million for two commissioned research papers on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and leadership. Barak completed only one. The Foundation justified full payment by stating the completed work was “sufficient.” Critically, Epstein served as de facto CFO of the Wexner family office during this exact period and controlled grant approvals. Whether Epstein specifically authorized or influenced this payment is unconfirmed, but the institutional mechanism for him to do so was in place.

Carbyne/Reporty investment (2014–2019): Epstein invested in Carbyne through his Southern Trust Company (STC), which held 66.67% of the investment vehicle SUM (E.B.) Limited Partnership. Barak served as general partner with carried interest. The corporate structure was deliberately layered: STC (U.S. Virgin Islands) invested into SUM (E.B.) LP (Israel), which invested into Carbyne Ltd. (Israel). When Israeli lawyers handling Carbyne’s anti-money-laundering compliance sought to identify STC’s beneficial owner, Epstein’s attorney Darren Indyke resisted disclosure, attempting to shield Epstein’s identity as the controlling person. Additionally, STC wired $1 million to ERGO (E.B. 2014) Ltd., another Barak-associated Israeli entity.

Real estate footprint: ACRIS records reveal Barak’s New York City property transactions: a Manhattan Club timeshare at 200 W 56th St purchased in May 2007 for $13,000 and sold post-Epstein arrest in September 2019 for $100; a Tribeca property at 15 Hubert St acquired in February 2017 for $3.1 million and sold a year later for $2.57 million; and a $3.7 million Ariel West condo at 245 W 99th St purchased in April 2025. The timing of the timeshare disposal—sold for a nominal $100 weeks after Epstein’s July 2019 arrest—warrants scrutiny as a potential effort to shed traceable assets.

sections.title: Carbyne and Surveillance Technology
sections.content:
Barak served as chairman of Carbyne (originally Reporty Homeland Security), an Israeli emergency call-handling technology company. Carbyne’s product enabled video streaming and location tracking from callers to 911 dispatch centers. While marketed as civilian safety technology, the company’s Israeli defense and intelligence pedigree—and its investor base—placed it at the intersection of surveillance capability and geopolitical access.

Epstein was actively involved in Carbyne’s business operations, not merely as a passive investor. Emails show Barak forwarding Carbyne exhibition notices to Epstein and Nicole Junkermann (April 2017: “Carbyne to Exhibit in American Security Expo 2017”). Business emails reference “Reporty advances report re New Investment” (February 2016) and “Touch Base re Reporty JE” (December 2014). Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund also invested in Carbyne, creating a node where Israeli intelligence expertise, Epstein capital, and Silicon Valley surveillance technology converged.

The most revealing episode involved Barak’s pitch of Carbyne for Qatar 2022 World Cup security. In late 2018, Epstein introduced Barak to Jabor Al Thani, who brokered a meeting between Barak and former Qatari Prime Minister Hamad bin Jassim Al Thani in London (December 20, 2018, at 100 Knightsbridge). Barak offered to “minimize the Israeli profile” of the technology—a remarkable proposition from a former Israeli Prime Minister, effectively acknowledging that the product’s Israeli intelligence associations were a commercial liability that required active concealment. A formal Carbyne 911 presentation for Qatar followed on January 1, 2019.

sections.title: Geopolitical Broker Role
sections.content:
The DOJ email corpus reveals Barak functioning as a geopolitical intelligence source for Epstein, reporting on meetings with heads of state, central bankers, and intelligence officials. This was not casual conversation between friends—it was structured, proactive intelligence reporting.

Russia (SPIEF, June 2015): Barak attended the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum and reported directly to Epstein on meetings with Russia’s most senior officials: Central Bank Governor Elvira Nabiullina, Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, former Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin, VTB Chairman Andrei Kostin, and Sberbank CEO Herman Gref. Most significantly, Barak met an individual identified only as “SS” (likely Vladislav Surkov or Igor Sechin) who “expressed interest in finding some area for actual cooperation. I proposed that we will discuss it with you.” The implication is clear: Barak was positioning Epstein as a counterparty for cooperation with senior Russian state actors.

Gulf states: Epstein brokered Barak’s access to Qatari leadership through Jabor Al Thani (introduced November 2018). Barak also maintained connections to Sultan bin Sulayem (chairman of DP World, Dubai) across both social and intelligence dimensions. Epstein further brokered Barak’s connection to Tom Barrack (September 2010), who served as a bridge to Gulf sovereign wealth and later to the Trump political orbit.

U.S. political figures: Epstein arranged a dinner with Steve Bannon and Barak on March 22, 2018, with further discussions in May 2018. Tom Pritzker sought meetings with Barak through Epstein (“I want to see Ehud to hear him on Obama Kerry,” December 2016). Lawrence Summers appeared in Barak’s network. These introductions positioned Barak as Epstein’s conduit to Israeli strategic perspective for American political and financial elites—a service that had clear value in both directions.

sections.title: Communication Infrastructure
sections.content:
The 1,411-file Barak email corpus (ehbarak1@gmail.com) is the single largest bilateral correspondence in the investigation, exceeding even the extensive Wolff (303 emails), Kathy Ruemmler (201), and Landon Thomas Jr. (185) archives. The volume alone signals a relationship of sustained operational intensity, not occasional social contact.

The scheduling infrastructure was formalized and routinized. Nili Priell Barak, Ehud’s wife, served as the dedicated intermediary for all meeting arrangements. Epstein’s assistant Lesley Groff emailed Nili directly to coordinate Barak’s schedule. When training a new assistant, Groff explained the protocol explicitly: “Jeffrey will probably want to see Ehud while he is in NY. Nili is Barak’s wife and I always email her to make/confirm appts for Ehud.” This was not ad hoc—it was standard operating procedure, with Nili functioning as a permanent scheduling channel.

Documented scheduling examples span years: May 2017 (“may we please scoot Ehud to 5pm”), June 2017 (“Yes he can call Ehud’s cell”), November 2017 (“Does Jeffrey’s schedule match Ehud’s in NY” leading to a breakfast or lunch on November 28). Nili also proactively curated Israeli media for Epstein’s consumption: in May 2011, she forwarded a translated Haaretz interview with Barak about “peace, politics, and Patek Philippe,” noting it “may be of interest to Jeffrey.” Epstein’s staff confirmed receipt. This bidirectional information flow—Barak’s Israeli media positioning fed to Epstein, Epstein’s introductions and capital fed to Barak—defined the relationship’s operational structure.
